title: Mark Clark's secret landing
body:
An American general paddled ashore in a canoe at night, hid in a wine cellar from the police, and went home without his trousers. It was one of the most important secret meetings of the war.

22 October 1942. Major General Mark Clark landed from the British submarine HMS Seraph near Cherchell, Algeria. At a seaside villa he met French General Charles Mast and U.S. diplomat Robert Murphy. Clark needed the French army in North Africa to help the coming Allied landings, not fight them.

Mast agreed. Then the local police, tipped off by the servants, came knocking. The Americans dropped into the cellar while their hosts faked a drunken party upstairs.

Escaping in heavy surf, Clark stripped off his trousers so the gold coins in his money belt would not drag him under. A canoe was lost, and the gold with it. Clark made it back to Seraph. Seventeen days later came Operation Torch.
photoNote: HMS Seraph, the submarine that carried Clark to Cherchell, entering harbor with crew on deck. Imperial War Museum wartime official photograph (British official WWII photos are out of Crown Copyright), copy from USNI Naval History, April 2023, supplied by Brian 16 Oct 2026. Likely Seraph's return to Portsmouth, Dec 1943 (IWM A 21106 series); exact catalogue number not confirmed. Replaces a Nov 1942 portrait of Clark (Truman Library 99-216) and before that a postwar portrait.

sources.title: Contact, USNI Naval History, April 2023 (HMS Seraph photo, credit Imperial War Museum)

On 22 October 1942, Mark Clark paddled ashore in secret from the submarine HMS Seraph near Cherchell, Algeria, to win the French over before the Allied landings in North Africa. Then the police came knocking. Seventeen days later, Operation Torch began.

declassified.fact: HMS Seraph's secret work was far from over. On 30 April 1943, her commander, Lieutenant Bill Jewell, surfaced off Huelva, Spain, and slipped a dead man dressed as a British officer into the sea, carrying fake invasion plans. It was Operation Mincemeat, the deception remembered as the man who never was.
